description: Sensitive Hermes-first Legal / Compliance example: evidence-review loop that stays shadow-only, requires expert approval, and blocks legal decisions, risk acceptance, contract changes, access decisions, and external sends.

project.description: A local compliance workspace for rehearsing Hermes-routed questionnaire and evidence-review loops.
project.primaryGoal: Reduce questionnaire and evidence-review cycle time without automating legal judgment.
project.sourceOfTruth: The compliance evidence register is authoritative; policy pages and contract summaries are approved inputs only after redaction.

answers.source_of_truth: The compliance evidence register defines approved control evidence; legal counsel owns interpretations.
answers.event_sources_subjects: Hermes receives Vanta questionnaire.requested events keyed by compliance request ID.

answers.trigger_or_cadence: A questionnaire request or policy exception review arrives through Hermes.
answers.problem_signal: A compliance questionnaire asks for evidence or policy language that must be answered from approved sources.
answers.pain_type_severity: Manual evidence gathering is slow, but wrong legal interpretation or external send would be critical risk.
answers.baseline: Two business days average response preparation time

answers.desired_automation_mode: monitor and draft evidence packets only
answers.read_write_boundary: Read approved evidence and draft packets only; no external send, legal interpretation, risk acceptance, exception approval, access approval, or contract change.

answers.guardrail_metric: zero unapproved external answers or legal interpretations
answers.baseline_target: Reduce preparation time from two business days to one day while preserving expert review.

answers.urgency_priority: Regulatory or customer deadline requests are urgent but never bypass expert review.
answers.pilot_scope: two recurring questionnaire types with redacted evidence bundles
answers.management_summary: weekly count of blocked requests, review cycle time, and missing-evidence reasons
